page: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Gen9 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.47 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 623.71 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read operations reaching 6484.12 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 188.26 GB/sec. Database and web serving benchmarks are also notable, with static web serving throughput measured at 103.35 GB/sec and Redis SET operations reaching 136.88 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and uncached large-block write memory bandwidth remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.12xlarge offers high compute density and strong multi-threaded performance per resource unit, typical of the Graviton ARM architecture. The primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and lack of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy graphics processing or massive deep learning training. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio also makes it less suitable for memory-bound applications. It is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, including high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data compression, database operations, and lightweight LLM prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. It features 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, but provides a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show top-tier capabilities in multi-threaded decompression, static web serving at 103.35 GB/sec, and Redis operations at 136.88 million operations per second. While single-core performance and large-block memory writes are average, its high multi-core efficiency makes it highly cost-effective for compute-heavy tasks. This server is best suited for high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and database workloads.
